Package org.aristonis.diwan.database.schema

Class ColumnDefinition

java.lang.Object
org.aristonis.diwan.database.schema.ColumnDefinition
Direct Known Subclasses:
ForeignIdColumnDefinition
public class ColumnDefinition extends Object
One column of a Blueprint, with Laravel's modifiers.

Each modifier returns this definition, so calls chain: table.string("email").nullable().unique(). Columns are not null unless nullable() is called.

A definition is changed only inside the schema callback. Once the schema builder has checked the blueprint, the definition is frozen and every modifier throws IllegalStateException, so a grammar cannot change what it compiles.

The class is open only to ForeignIdColumnDefinition; its constructor is not public.

    • defaultValue

      public ColumnDefinition defaultValue(Object value)
      Sets the value the database stores when an insert leaves the column out.

      Named defaultValue because default is a Java keyword.

      Parameters:
      value - the value: a String, a Boolean, an integer type, BigInteger, BigDecimal, a finite Float or Double, or an Expression; null sets SQL NULL as the default, as Laravel's default(null) does
      Returns:
      this definition
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the value has another type or is not finite
      IllegalStateException - if the definition is frozen

    • useCurrent

      public ColumnDefinition useCurrent()
      Makes the database's current date or time the default.
      Returns:
      this definition
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if the column is not a date, time or year column, or the definition is frozen
      API Note:
      On a year column the grammar writes the database's way of reading the current year, so defaultValue() stays empty there; usesCurrent() tells it apart.

    • unique

      public ColumnDefinition unique(boolean isWanted)
      Drops or keeps this column's conventionally named unique index when the column is changed.

      unique(true) is the same as unique(); unique(false) drops the index named <table>_<column>_unique and is allowed only together with change(). On SQLite a unique constraint written inside the table definition is not an index and cannot be dropped this way.

      Parameters:
      isWanted - false to drop the index
      Returns:
      this definition
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if the definition is frozen

    • check

      public ColumnDefinition check(String sql)
      Adds a CHECK constraint on this column. Several checks are kept in the order given.

      The SQL is written into the statement as given, like an Expression: build it from constants only, never from user input. On SQLite, adding a checked column to an existing table copies the whole table, so add such columns in one Schema.table call.

      Parameters:
      sql - the condition, without the check keyword or outer parentheses, never null or blank
      Returns:
      this definition
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if sql is null
      IllegalArgumentException - if sql is blank
      IllegalStateException - if the definition is frozen

    • change

      public ColumnDefinition change()
      Redefines the existing column with this name instead of adding a new one.

      The new definition replaces the old one in full: a modifier that is not stated again, such as nullable() or a default, is gone after the change. On SQLite every change rebuilds the table and copies all its rows, so put the changes for one table in one Schema.table call. An auto-increment column cannot be changed.

      Returns:
      this definition
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if the definition is frozen

    • precision

      public OptionalInt precision()
      Returns the column's precision.

      For ColumnType.FLOAT it is the binary digits of the mantissa, 1 to 53; for the time and timestamp types it is the fractional-second digits, 0 to 6. Other types have none.

      Returns:
      the precision, or empty when none was set or the type has none

    • isNotNullStated

      public boolean isNotNullStated()
      Tells whether nullable(false) was called.

      Grammars use it for generated columns, which, as in Laravel, are not marked not null unless asked: their value follows the columns they are computed from.

      Returns:
      true after nullable(false)
